overview.overview:
Minnesota is projected to back the Democratic presidential nominee in 2028 by an expected margin of about 9.5 points. The state voted Democratic in 2020 and 2024, though its margin narrowed from 7.1 points to 4.2 points between those elections. Minnesota typically runs about five points more Democratic than the nation as a whole.

The projected range is wide, from a tie to a Democratic lead of roughly 19 points, but a close result looks unlikely, and the state is unlikely to decide the Electoral College. The national environment currently leans Democratic, and the 2026 statewide readings for Senate and governor also point to a Democratic advantage. No state-level polls are included in the current data.
overview.watch: A marked narrowing of the national environment or a sustained drop in Democratic support among suburban and rural voters could shrink the expected margin considerably.
key_factors: Democratic voting in the last two presidential elections, although the 2024 margin was narrower than in 2020
A lean about five points more Democratic than the nation
A Democratic-leaning national environment and favorable 2026 statewide readings
